samples.text:
The chart shows how many people visited five tourist attractions in a city in the years 2010 and 2020.

In 2010, the castle was the most popular attraction with 640,000 visitors. The science museum had 410,000 visitors and the aquarium had 350,000. The botanic gardens and the art gallery had less visitors, 280,000 and 190,000.

In 2020, some attractions became more popular and some became less popular. The science museum increase a lot to 590,000, and it become the most visited place. The art gallery also went up to 260,000 and the botanic gardens rose slightly to 300,000. On the other hand, the castle visitors fell down to 520,000. The biggest change was the aquarium, which dropped from 350,000 to only 150,000, so it was the least popular attraction in 2020.

Overall, the science museum, the art gallery and the botanic gardens got more visitors, but the castle and the aquarium got less. The science museum replaced the castle as the most popular attraction.
samples.why: All figures accurate · overview present but placed at the end · year-by-year listing with simple linking · some informal or awkward word choices · verb-form and quantifier errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares the number of people who visited five attractions in a city in 2010 and 2020.

Overall, the science museum, the botanic gardens and the art gallery all attracted more visitors over the decade, while visitor numbers at the castle and the aquarium declined. As a result, the science museum replaced the castle as the city's most popular attraction.

In 2010, the castle was clearly the most visited site, with 640,000 visitors, followed by the science museum at 410,000. However, by 2020 the castle's figure had fallen to 520,000, whereas the science museum saw a significant rise to 590,000. The art gallery also became more popular, with visitor numbers increasing by 70,000 to 260,000, and the botanic gardens experienced a slight growth, from 280,000 to 300,000.

The most dramatic change took place at the aquarium. Having attracted 350,000 people in 2010, it welcomed only 150,000 in 2020, a fall of more than half, which meant it went from being the third most popular attraction to the least popular one.
samples.why: Clear overview of rises, falls and the change at the top · key features highlighted with accurate figures · logical grouping and cohesive devices · good collocations · one minor article slip.

samples.text:
The chart illustrates visitor numbers at five of a city's tourist attractions in 2010 and 2020.

Over the ten-year period, the popularity of the attractions shifted noticeably. The science museum overtook the castle to become the most visited site and the aquarium suffered a steep decline, whereas the botanic gardens and the art gallery both gained visitors.

The castle attracted 640,000 visitors in 2010, the highest figure for either year, but this dropped by 120,000 to 520,000 in 2020. Over the same period, the science museum enjoyed the largest increase of any attraction, with visitor numbers climbing by 180,000, from 410,000 to 590,000, which made it the clear leader by the end of the decade.

The aquarium's decline was even more pronounced than the castle's. Its visitor numbers fell from 350,000 to just 150,000, less than half the original figure, leaving it with the smallest audience of all five attractions by 2020. By contrast, the art gallery grew from 190,000 to 260,000, while the botanic gardens remained relatively stable, rising marginally from 280,000 to 300,000, and consequently moved above the aquarium in the rankings.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected and logically grouped · clear overview · figures used selectively with accurate derived changes · cohesion managed well · wide, precise vocabulary · error-free complex sentences.
